newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: "Millenium bug" to boost computer demand, says NEC.
newsitem.headline: "Millenium bug" to boost computer demand, says NEC.

text.p: The so-called millenium bug will boost demand for computers over the next two years, but a shortage of software engineers to deal with it is a headache, a senior NEC executive said on Friday.
"There will be a rush in demand (for both hardware and new software) next year and the following year," Noel Hon Chia Chun, Managing Director of NEC Singapore, said in an interview.
Hon told Reuters NEC was talking with small businesses to upgrade their relatively old computer systems and software to solve the millenium issue.
"We expect higher revenues (from such businesses)," he said, but declined to provide an estimate.

The millenium bug results from computer systems using two digit to show the year. At the turn of the century, many computers will show 00 for the year and interpret it as 1900, potentially creating havoc.
Large organisations with new mainframe systems will be relatively unaffected by the bug issue because they will be taken care of by new applications software, he said.
But Hon said a major concern was a manpower shortage.
NEC Corp launched a special task force last year to tackle the millenium problem and allied with two Indian companies for the development of software.

NEC will add one more Indian software developing company for the project shortly, raising the total number of engineers engaged in the development of software for NEC to 500 by the end of this year, an NEC spokesman said.
